results.title: Truth-table evaluation
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Given a Boolean valuation $v$ of the atoms, the truth value of a proposition is computed recursively: an atom $x$ has value $v(x)$, $A \wedge B$ is true iff both $A$ and $B$ are, $A \vee B$ is true iff at least one of them is, and $A \to B$ is true iff $A$ is false or $B$ is true. Falsum $\bot$, when present, is itself an atom, so its value $v(\bot)$ is part of the valuation and need not be false.

results.title: Truth value of a negation
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Suppose the atoms include a distinguished atom $\bot$, and let $v$ be a Boolean valuation of the atoms with $v(\bot) = \mathrm{false}$. Then for every proposition $A$, the truth-table value under $v$ of $\neg A$, defined as $A \to \bot$, is the Boolean negation of the truth-table value of $A$ under $v$.

results.title: Truth-table consequence
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $T$ be a theory (a set of propositions), $\Gamma$ a context (a finite set of propositions) and $A$ a proposition. Then $A$ is a truth-table consequence of $\Gamma$ in $T$ when every Boolean valuation of the atoms under which all members of $T$ and all members of $\Gamma$ evaluate to true also makes $A$ evaluate to true.

results.title: Soundness of natural deduction for truth tables
results.caption: Theorem

results.title: Truth-table soundness of derivability
results.caption: Theorem

results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A group $P$ is a generalized quaternion group if, for some natural number $k \ge 1$, it is isomorphic to the quaternion group $Q_{2^{k+2}} = \langle a, x \mid a^{2^{k+1}} = 1,\ x^2 = a^{2^k},\ x^{-1} a x = a^{-1} \rangle$ of order $2^{k+2}$. results.title: Dedekind domains as the Noetherian domains where to contain is to divide
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: An integral domain $A$ is a Dedekind domain if and only if $A$ is Noetherian and, for all ideals $I$ and $J$ of $A$, $I$ divides $J$ if and only if $J \subseteq I$.

results.title: Dedekind domains via principal products
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: An integral domain $A$ is a Dedekind domain if and only if for every nonzero ideal $I$ of $A$ there is an ideal $J$ of $A$ such that $IJ$ is a nonzero principal ideal.

results.title: Equivalent characterizations of Dedekind domains
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For an integral domain $A$, the following are equivalent: (1) $A$ is a Dedekind domain; (2) $A$ is Noetherian and, for all ideals $I$ and $J$ of $A$, $I$ divides $J$ if and only if $J \subseteq I$; (3) for every nonzero ideal $I$ of $A$ there is an ideal $J$ of $A$ such that $IJ$ is a nonzero principal ideal.

results.title: Dedekind domains are the integrally closed Noetherian domains of dimension at most one
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $A$ be a Noetherian integral domain. Then $A$ is integrally closed and has Krull dimension at most one if and only if $A$ is a Dedekind domain.

results.title: DVR localizations in a Noetherian domain

results.title: Quotients of Dedekind domains by nonzero ideals are principal ideal rings

results.title: Domains with principal quotients are Noetherian

results.title: Principal quotients give discrete valuation rings at nonzero primes

results.title: Dedekind domains from principal quotients
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $A$ be an integral domain such that for every nonzero ideal $I$ of $A$ the quotient ring $A/I$ is a principal ideal ring. Then $A$ is a Dedekind domain.

results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $p$ be a joint probability law on $\alpha \times \beta$ with $\alpha$ and $\beta$ finite, the law of an attribute $X$ (first coordinate) and a label $Y$ (second coordinate). The information gain of splitting on $X$ for predicting $Y$ is the real number $H(Y) - H(Y \mid X)$, where $H(Y)$ is the Shannon entropy in bits of the marginal law of $Y$ and $H(Y \mid X)$ is the conditional entropy in bits of $Y$ given…

results.title: Information gain in terms of entropies
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $p$ be a joint probability law on $\alpha \times \beta$ with $\alpha$ and $\beta$ finite, and let $p_X$ and $p_Y$ be its marginal laws on $\alpha$ and on $\beta$. Writing $H$ for Shannon entropy in bits, the information gain of $p$ equals $H(p_X) + H(p_Y) - H(p)$.

results.title: No split has negative information gain
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every joint probability law $p$ on $\alpha \times \beta$ with $\alpha$ and $\beta$ finite, the information gain of $p$ is at least $0$.

results.title: Information gain is mutual information
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\alpha$ and $\beta$ be finite sets carrying σ-algebras in which singletons are measurable, and let $p$ be a joint probability law on $\alpha \times \beta$. The information gain of $p$, regarded as an element of $[0, \infty]$, equals the mutual information in bits of $p$ viewed as a probability measure on $\alpha \times \beta$.

results.title: Zero information gain means independence
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\alpha$ and $\beta$ be finite sets carrying σ-algebras in which singletons are measurable, and let $p$ be a joint probability law on $\alpha \times \beta$. The information gain of $p$ is zero if and only if $p$, as a measure, equals the product of its marginal law on $\alpha$ and its marginal law on $\beta$; that is, exactly when the attribute (first coordinate) and the label (second coordinate) are independent.

results.title: Euclid P-position test
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For natural numbers $a$ and $b$, the Euclid P-position test at $(a, b)$ is the value at $(a, b)$ of the fuel-bounded evaluation of the P-positions of Euclid with fuel $a + b$.

results.title: Euclid moves
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The moves of Euclid from a pair $(a, b)$ of natural numbers are as follows. If $a = b$, $a = 0$ or $b = 0$, there are none. If $0 < a < b$, the moves are to the pairs $(a, b - ja)$ for every integer $j \ge 1$ with $ja < b$; if $0 < b < a$, the moves are to the pairs $(a - jb, b)$ for every integer $j \ge 1$ with $jb < a$.

results.title: Euclid moves lower the sum
